macro: US equity futures are nearly flat Wednesday morning — S&P +0.05%, Dow +0.02%, Nasdaq -0.04%, and Russell 2000 -0.27%. Asian markets were mixed, with Hong Kong down roughly 1% dragged by Alibaba (-4.4%) and Tencent (-2.4%), while Korea and Taiwan outperformed. Treasuries are flat across the curve, the market is pricing ~33 basis points of hikes this year and ~45 basis points in 2027, Brent is flat near $99.50, gold is down 1.0%, silver down 2.5%, and bitcoin off 0.4%.
market_outlook: Adam's focus today is squarely on two catalysts: progress in US-Iran nuclear negotiations (which could meaningfully move oil and broaden market risk sentiment) and Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote at 7pm ET (where investors expect bullish commentary on Muse adoption and the forthcoming Watermelon frontier model). The tape is cautiously constructive but directionless ahead of these events, with pick-and-shovels/semis buoyed by AI enthusiasm while financials, software, and select consumer names face pressure from Muse disruption fears. Key earnings before the open — CTAS, GIS, PAYX — plus the MCD analyst meeting and US flash PMIs at 9:45am ET round out the morning agenda.

company_items.summary: Zuckerberg delivers the Meta Connect keynote tonight at 7pm ET, with investors expecting bullish commentary on Muse adoption (500K+ users and 250K+ DAUs just one week post-launch) and the forthcoming Watermelon frontier model. The Connect conference has historically focused on smart glasses, but AI is the dominant narrative for the stock. OpenAI's Dev Day is approaching and could launch a competing Muse-like personal agent.

KBH reported decent FQ3 EPS upside at $1.05 vs. the Street's $0.89, driven largely by cost controls (SG&A ratio beat by ~0.30%) and modestly better deliveries and gross margins. However, the FQ4 guide is mixed-to-underwhelming — deliveries roughly inline but gross margin and SG&A ratio both worse than expected. Management cited a challenging housing market with conditions weakening since June, higher mortgage rates pressuring affordability, and broader geopolitical uncertainty.

China may issue formal guidance ordering data centers to reduce their use of Broadcom hardware as Beijing pushes the tech industry toward domestic alternatives. This is a meaningful demand-side risk for AVGO's China revenue. No formal announcement has been made yet but the FT report adds headline overhang to the stock.

RCL confirmed it will acquire a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts for $3 billion, representing a forward EBITDA multiple of approximately 10x. Management says the deal will be accretive to earnings next year. The move expands RCL's land-based resort footprint and diversifies its hospitality offering.

BHF shares rallied in the final minutes of Tuesday's session after Bloomberg reported that Sixth Street remains interested in acquiring BHF should the Acquarian deal fall apart. This provides a potential M&A floor under the stock and renewed takeout speculation. The situation remains fluid with no formal deal announced.
company_items.catalyst: M&A speculation (Sixth Street interest reported by Bloomberg)

company_items.summary: NFLX shares were hit Tuesday after receiving its second analyst downgrade in a week — HSBC cut to Hold, following Wells Fargo's Underweight downgrade on September 18. Investor sentiment is deteriorating on concerns about engagement trends and a weak content lineup. Netflix reports earnings on October 20.

LH shares fell 3% Tuesday amid concerns over reduced CMS Medicare payment rates. Management characterized the new rates as imposing steep annual payment cuts that threaten patient access to lab services, though the company is reaffirming its 2026-2029 long-term guidance issued at the September 10 analyst meeting. Specific 2027 guidance impact will be communicated in February alongside Q4 earnings.

WOR reported modest FQ1 upside with EPS of 82 cents vs. the Street's 75 cents, EBITDA of $74MM vs. $69.5MM expected, and sales up 13% to $344MM vs. the $332MM estimate. Management highlighted rapidly growing demand for engineered ASME tanks used in liquid cooling systems for data centers as a key growth driver. Results suggest early-cycle momentum in fiscal 2027.
company_items.catalyst: Earnings beat (FQ1 EPS, EBITDA, and revenue all above consensus)

company_items.summary: Jana Partners is pressing the Six Flags board to explore a sale of the company. The activist campaign adds event-driven upside optionality to the stock. No formal process has been announced, but Jana's involvement typically signals meaningful pressure for strategic action.
company_items.catalyst: Activist investor (Jana Partners calling for sale)

company_items.summary: Microsoft is expanding bulk discount offers to corporate Copilot buyers and preparing to launch a refreshed 'super app' version of Copilot — potentially as soon as this week — that combines coding tools and personal AI agents. The move signals Microsoft is accelerating AI monetization efforts amid intensifying competition from Meta's Muse and OpenAI. This is both a competitive and commercial development to watch.
company_items.catalyst: Product launch / competitive positioning (Copilot super app imminent)

sectors: Financials came under pressure Tuesday on fears that Meta's Muse AI agent could disrupt sub-industries like retail brokers and wealth managers. Refinery stocks sold off after Trump signaled support for a diesel export ban. Software/services names including ADBE, BKNG, and INTU face renewed disruption fears from the success of Muse and anticipation of further AI agents launching in coming weeks. Semis and AI pick-and-shovels have been buoyed by Muse enthusiasm over the last several sessions. Homebuilders are cautious — KBH macro commentary cited weakening conditions, higher mortgage rates, and geopolitical uncertainty weighing on buyer confidence.

Here's your morning game plan for Wednesday, September 23rd.

Futures are essentially flat coming into the open. S&P is up about five basis points, the Dow is barely positive, the Nasdaq is slightly negative, and the Russell 2000 is underperforming, down about a quarter of a percent. Asia was mixed overnight — Hong Kong dragged lower by Alibaba, down four and a half percent, and Tencent, down two and a half percent. Europe is quiet, flat to down a tenth of a percent. Treasuries are unchanged, Brent crude is flat just under a hundred dollars, gold is off one percent, and silver is getting hit hard, down two and a half percent.

The two things driving everything right now are Iran and Meta. On Iran, Trump said Tuesday afternoon that US and Iranian delegations had a very productive three-hour meeting at the UN. Markets want to see Brent keep coming down — if that happens, you get lower yields, lower inflation, better margins, better consumer confidence. The whole macro picture improves. But bears will tell you the region is still nowhere near pre-war conditions, and Russia-Ukraine remains on an escalatory path with no ceasefire in sight.

On the company side — the Meta Connect keynote tonight at seven pm Eastern is the single biggest catalyst of the day. Zuckerberg is expected to deliver bullish commentary on Muse adoption — the AI agent already has over five hundred thousand users in its first week — and update investors on the Watermelon frontier model. Pick-and-shovels and semis have been running hard on Muse enthusiasm. Watch for OpenAI to potentially counter with its own agent at Dev Day next Tuesday.

Broadcom is a name to watch on the downside — the FT is reporting China may formally order data centers to reduce Broadcom hardware usage in favor of domestic alternatives. That's a real demand risk for AVGO in China.

Royal Caribbean confirmed the Sandals acquisition — fifty percent stake for three billion dollars at roughly ten times forward EBITDA, and management says it's accretive next year. Bullish for RCL.

KB Home beat on FQ3 earnings — a dollar five versus the Street's eighty-nine cents — but the FQ4 guide disappointed on gross margin and SG&A, and the macro commentary was cautious. Mixed read for homebuilders broadly.

Netflix is under pressure after a second downgrade in a week, this time from HSBC. Sentiment is clearly deteriorating on engagement concerns heading into October twentieth earnings.

Worthington Enterprises beat across the board on FQ1 — EPS, EBITDA, and revenue all above consensus — with management calling out surging demand for data center liquid cooling tanks. Clean beat, bullish.

Before the open this morning watch Cintas, General Mills, and Paychex earnings, followed by the MCD analyst day at nine-thirty and flash PMIs at nine forty-five. The real event is tonight's Zuckerberg keynote. This tape is in a holding pattern until then.
